summary: Rapid tenant retry stampede after auth cache eviction triggering 5xx errors and upstream runtime restarts
description:
Issue summary:
A NovaDocs tenant experienced a rapid elevation in 5xx responses from the public API starting ~2026-03-13T15:05Z. Error rates spiked to ~18% for requests routed to us-east for a ~45 minute window. Customers reported streaming disconnects and bulk-embedding uploads failing with upstream 502/503 responses.

Impact:
- NovaDocs (dedicated) saw production traffic for several routes fail, causing degraded UX in their document ingestion pipeline.
- Elevated token billing and retries observed from NovaDocs client side.
- Platform-wide ingress error floor briefly rose for us-east affecting a small number of other tenants routed to the same edge pool.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (edge + apigw cluster a1)
- Dedicated runtime pool: rdw-dedicated-us-east-03 (GPU A100 pool)
- Affected model: redwood-rlhf-7b pinned by customer

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) NovaDocs started a bulk embedding upload (chunked POST, ~2.5k chunks) at 2026-03-13T15:02Z.
2) During the upload the platform rotated an internal auth cache (shortened TTL due to a recent config change) which caused cached tokens used by the apigw to be evicted ~15:04Z.
3) The client retried aggressively (retry window set to immediate 3x by their SDK) causing a concentrated burst to the same upstream runtime shards.
4) The serving runtime entered a hot prefetch/pinning state; concurrent prefetches increased GPU memory pressure and led to several GPU processes OOM-ing and restarting (NVML driver logs show multiple resets).
5) API Gateway started returning 502/503 as upstreams died and the ingress rate limiter began shedding.

Logs / signals collected:
- apigw logs (apigw-a1): repeated 502/503 responses correlated with retries from NovaDocs client IP range.
- auth-cache metrics: cache_evictions spike at 15:04Z tied to TTL sweep job (config change: auth_cache.ttl_seconds = 30 -> 10).
- runtime logs (rdw-dedicated-us-east-03): NVML reset entries and "OOM: allocation failed" stack traces at 15:06-15:12Z.
- Prometheus: request_retries_total for NovaDocs route increased 8x; runtime_gpu_memory_free dropped below safe threshold before restarts.
- Tracing: spike in hedged retries and hedged_miss ratios for the route.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: Auth cache eviction created a synchronized retry window across many in-flight clients which amplified traffic to the same runtime shards.
- Hypothesis 2: Customer SDK retry settings (immediate retries x3) converted transient 401/5xx into a stampede.
- Observed that the runtime prefetcher aggressively attempts to prime KV cache on retry bursts; combined with pinned model and large sequence length in embedding chunks this pushed GPU memory over threshold.
- Cross-referenced slack thread #support-novadocs (link: slack://channel/support-novadocs) and SRE alerting timelines (PagerDuty: PDINC-8813).
- Related internal task INT-4221 tracks auth_cache TTL change that was rolled out last night.

Temporary mitigation applied (15:18Z):
- Rotated route weights to send NovaDocs traffic to warm fallback pool (rdw-dedicated-us-east-05) which had spare capacity.
- Increased auth-cache TTL back to safe value (30s) and paused TTL sweep job.
- Applied ingress circuit-breaker: per-tenant retry throttling and exponential-backoff enforcement at apigw layer.
- Eng also patched serving-runtime to reduce prefetch aggressiveness under heavy retry rates (hotfix PR referenced below).

Resolution and follow-ups:
- Status: customer traffic stabilized by 15:30Z after weight shift and TTL revert; runtime restarts subsided as prefetch load decreased.
- Root cause: combination of auth-cache TTL regression + aggressive client retry policy + prefetch behavior causing transient GPU OOMs.
- Permanent actions planned:
  * Revert auth_cache.ttl_seconds config permanently and add canary gating for TTL sweeps (owner: INT infra config team).
  * Add a server-side jitter/backoff enforcement for known retrying SDKs and strengthen per-tenant ingress backpressure controls (owner: api-gateway team).
  * Modify serving runtime prefetch to degrade more gracefully under high retry density; add a threshold to abort prefetch when GPU free memory < X% (owner: runtime team, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4213).
  * Customer guidance: recommend NovaDocs update SDK retry policy to exponential backoff and add client-side jitter. Support to follow up with recommended config.
- Postmortem planned; tentative owner: Marcus Li. Target postmortem publish date: 2026-03-18.
